cohort: The study included 531 pregnant women who underwent labor induction at the National Guard Hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between January and April 2023.
finding: Labor induction success was primarily predicted by increasing parity and Prostin administration, while lower gravidity (<=3) and Propess medication were associated with increased operative procedures.
mod_finding: Normal deliveries accounted for 62% of births (indicating IOL success), while 31.1% resulted in cesarean deliveries (indicating IOL failure), with lower gravidity (<=3) and Propess medication associated with a higher likelihood of operative delivery.
